critiques.description: thr-001 treats it as established that an arbitrary Internet-based attacker can send deployment webhook requests to the Event Receiver’s public URL, but the cited documentation only states that the receiver is a "public" HTTPS endpoint used by the external CI platform; it does not document whether access is restricted (e.g., via IP allowlists or firewalls).
critiques.rationale: Precondition 3 and the threat description rely on the claim that an Internet-based attacker can send HTTP requests with arbitrary JSON bodies to the Event Receiver. evd-002 describes the Event Receiver as "A public HTTPS endpoint that the external CI platform calls" and evd-003 refers to the receiver’s "public URL", but neither passage specifies whether other Internet clients (beyond the CI platform) can reach the endpoint or whether network access controls constrain who can connect. Evidence assessment eas-038 already notes that the mechanics of forged events are supported but that this specific precondition about attacker reachability is not fully established by the documentation. Because network reachability materially affects whether the stated Internet-attacker scenario holds as written and whether the current "high" threat confidence is justified, additional documentation on network access controls (or an explicit statement that this is an assumption) is needed.
